review.brief_reason: Let P=cos(sin(2.655034*x1)), Q=cos(sin(3.61515*x1)). Original leading part: 0.000922 - 2.01486*(Q-P)/D = 0.000922 + 2.01486*(P-Q)/D, matching the proposed numerator. The denominator changes from sqrt(A)*sqrt(B) to sqrt(A*B). Here A = 2 + exp(...)/(sin(...))**2 >= 2 wherever defined (the only singularity is sin(...)=0, which makes both forms undefined identically), and B = 1 + (square)/(positive*positive) >= 1 always; the squared numerators match since (-cos(2.655034*x1)+Q)^2 = (Q-cos(2.655034*x1))^2. Thus A,B>0 on the common domain, so sqrt(A)*sqrt(B)=sqrt(A*B) exactly, denominators stay positive, and no sign/branch ambiguity arises. Same variable x1, same domain, fewer sqrt nodes (two sqrts merged into one) plus a cleaned sign, so it is simpler.
